examples.title: A landing page that scrolls sideways on phones
examples.prompt: Our landing page looks off on my iPhone and scrolls sideways. Check it on mobile and fix whatever breaks.
examples.summary: The SaaS landing page has 11 typical AI-built bugs: a 640px hero image, a 760px pricing table, an unbreakable API URL, a CTA on top of the logo, a cookie banner covering 57% of a small phone, tiny social icons and a squashed avatar. The sweep names the element behind each one with a cause hint. After fluid CSS fixes the same sweep comes back clean at all 8 widths, and --compare reports 66 issues fixed.
examples.command: node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/broken-page.html --full-page && node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/fixed-page.html --full-page --compare

media.alt: Two 375px screenshots side by side. Left: the header CTA overlaps the logo, the hero image runs 289px off-screen and a cookie banner covers most of the screen, all outlined in red and numbered. Right: the fixed page with the full logo row, a fitted hero image and a compact cookie bar.
media.caption: 375px before and after. Red boxes are errors and amber dashed boxes are warnings. The +289px marker shows how far the hero image runs off-screen.

media.alt: Two 375px screenshots further down the page. Left: an API URL and the pricing table run off the right edge (+53px, +409px) and the avatar is squashed. Right: the URL wraps, the table scrolls inside its own box and the avatar is round.
media.caption: Below the fold: the unbreakable URL gets overflow-wrap: anywhere, the pricing table moves into an overflow-x: auto wrapper and the avatar gets object-fit: cover.

media.alt: Top of the contact sheet: a list of findings grouped across widths, then annotated screenshots at 320, 375, 414, 768, 1024 and 1280px with error and warning counts and sideways-scroll amounts.
media.caption: The contact sheet the agent reads first: each finding listed once with the widths where it happens, then every viewport with its counts.

examples.title: An orders dashboard blown open by 1fr
examples.prompt: The orders dashboard scrolls sideways on my laptop and it's worse on mobile. Find out why and fix it properly, no overflow-x: hidden.
examples.summary: An app shell built as grid-template-columns: 232px 1fr lets a 10-column table stretch the main column, so the page scrolls sideways even at 1280px. Run 1 names main as the culprit, suggests minmax(0, 1fr), and lets main shrink for a moment to list what inside it would still overflow: the table, a filter row that doesn't wrap, and a KPI grid stretched by a long campaign tag. Run 2 (shell fixed) confirms those three, and run 3, with all four fixes, is clean at every width.
examples.command: node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/dashboard/broken.html --full-page && node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/dashboard/shell-fixed.html --full-page --compare && node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/dashboard/fixed.html --full-page --compare
examples.result: 6 errors (3 inner culprits named up front) → 12 → 0

media.alt: Dashboard at 1280px with a dark sidebar. The whole main column is outlined in red with a +135px marker, and the orders table's Status column is cut off at the right edge.
media.caption: Run 1, 1280px: the grid item main is wider than its 1fr track. Hint: use minmax(0, 1fr), plus the table, div.chips and section.kpis that would still overflow inside it.

media.alt: Two 375px screenshots. Left: three numbered red boxes for the KPI grid (+210px), the filter chips (+245px) and the orders table (+752px). Right: the KPI cards stacked in one column, the chips wrapped onto three rows and the table scrolling inside its card.
media.caption: Run 2 (shell fixed) names the table, section.kpis and div.chips. Run 3 adds a table scroll wrapper, auto-fit minmax(min(100%, 13rem), 1fr) KPI tracks and flex-wrap.

media.alt: Contact sheet for run 2: three grouped findings (table @320–1280, section.kpis @320–414, div.chips @320–414) above annotated screenshots at six widths.
media.caption: Run 2 contact sheet: the table overflows up to 1280px, while the KPI grid and the chips only break on phones.

examples.title: A blog post with a runaway code block and hidden anchors
examples.prompt: Run a responsive QA pass on the edge-caching blog post before I publish it.
examples.summary: A long article with a fixed 72px header. A one-line <pre> widens the page at every width, the diagram has a CSS width of 720px, every table-of-contents link lands its heading under the header, and a width: 100vw band ends up wider than the page wherever a classic (Windows) scrollbar takes up room. Four small CSS fixes, including html { scroll-padding-top: 80px }, clear all 24 errors.
examples.command: node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/fixtures/blog.html --full-page && node scripts/sweep.mjs examples/blog/fixed.html --full-page --compare
examples.result: 24 errors at all 8 widths → 0 (24 fixed, 0 new)

media.alt: Two 375px screenshots of the article. Left: the heading is outlined inside a hatched strip marking where the fixed header lands after the #why jump, the code line runs 1056px off-screen and the diagram runs 365px off-screen. Right: the code block scrolls inside its dark box and the diagram fits the column.
media.caption: 375px before and after: the code block gets overflow-x: auto and the diagram becomes width: 100%; max-width: 720px.

media.alt: Two 375px screens right after jumping to #why. Left: the sweep's post-jump screenshot, where the fixed Devlog header (hatched) sits on top of the outlined heading and only the paragraph below is visible. Right: the fixed page after the same jump, with the heading in full view below the header.
media.caption: anchor-hidden also saves the screen right after the jump (shots/<page>/<w>x<h>-jump-<id>.png). Right: the fixed page after the same TOC click, with html { scroll-padding-top: 80px }.

media.alt: The article at 1280px. Top: the Why cache at the edge heading (1) sits inside a hatched strip showing what the fixed header covers after the jump, and the code line runs 444px off-screen (2). Bottom: the full-width blue newsletter band is outlined with a +8px marker (3).
media.caption: Desktop shows the bugs a Mac trackpad hides. The 15px classic scrollbar makes the 100vw band too wide, and every TOC jump lands under the fixed header.
